_comment: mcpServers sent inline in the Cursor Cloud Agents launch request (see
files on disk), this is the API's own shape: an ARRAY of server defs
with a 'type' discriminator. ${...} placeholders are substituted by
cursor-cloud.sh at launch time — nothing expands them in the VM, so a
missed substitution fails the clone/auth loudly instead of leaking.
The stdio command self-clones the MCP server source at an exact SHA
and builds it inside Cursor's VM: this keeps 'the server under test is
THIS source revision' true in the cloud (mcp_version: source), without
depending on how Cursor lays out repo checkouts on disk. Requirements
it places on the VM: git+go toolchains and GitHub egress. The build
runs at MCP-handshake time (cold: ~1-2 min); if Cursor's handshake
timeout proves too tight, move the clone+build into a
.cursor/environment.json install step on the scenario base branch and
leave only the exec here. Everything before exec is fenced to stderr:
stdout belongs to the MCP stdio protocol.

mcpServers.name: buildkite
args: if [ ! -x /tmp/bk-mcp-src/buildkite-mcp-server ]; then rm -rf /tmp/bk-mcp-src && git clone --quiet https://github.com/${MCP_SRC_REPO}.git /tmp/bk-mcp-src && git -C /tmp/bk-mcp-src checkout --quiet ${MCP_SRC_SHA} && (cd /tmp/bk-mcp-src && go build -o buildkite-mcp-server ./cmd/buildkite-mcp-server); fi 1>&2 && exec /tmp/bk-mcp-src/buildkite-mcp-server stdio --read-only
